openPoints: What is the operator-facing recovery procedure when strict startup validation refuses to open a corrupt but rebuildable SQLite index?
How is durability preserved if the filesystem error that caused a mirror append failure also prevents truncateSync or unlinkSync during rollback, which is currently best-effort?
Should graph.import validate the claims file even on its idempotent existing-bootstrap path, so a changed or corrupt source cannot be silently accepted while the in-memory graph is replaced?
architectureTip: Document an explicit JSONL-to-SQLite recovery command and evolve mirror batching toward an append journal with crash-recoverable commit markers.
topFinding: Retry #2 root-cause fixes all prior application-level findings: canonical rows are filtered before pagination, graph imports normalize before effects, standalone/import/TTL writers share rollbackable mirror transactions, deterministic second-append faults restore SQLite and mirrors, encoded traversal is denied, and Windows projection metrics are accurate; residual risk is operational crash/filesystem recovery hardening.
